articles.title: Patna HC cautions DMs, SPs against misuse of crime control law
articles.summary: Patna High Court quashes three externment orders, warns DMs/SPs on misuse of Bihar crime-control laws, and imposes Rs 3.9 lakh cost on state as compensation.
articles.body: By: Dev Kumar PandeyPATNA: The Patna high court has cautioned district magistrates (DMs) and superintendents of police (SPs) against declaring people “antisocial” without strictly following procedural norms, while imposing a total cost of Rs3.9 lakh on the state govt in three cases involving externment orders under Bihar’s crime control law.A division bench of Justices Rajeev Ranjan Prasad and Sunil Dutta Mishra passed the three orders on Sept 11 while quashing externment orders challenged through separate criminal writ petitions. The orders came into the public domain on Sept 12.In a petition filed by Chandan Kumar, an elected panchayati raj representative from Giriyak block in Nalanda district, the court quashed an externment order passed by the Nalanda DM. It directed Kumar to mark his attendance at Silao police station every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.The court imposed a cost of Rs60,000 on the state in the case as compensation to Kumar.In another petition filed by Shashi Kumar alias Fukan and Ajay Singh, both residents of a village under Katrisarai police station area in Nalanda, the court quashed an externment order dated Oct 10, 2025, passed by the Nalanda DM, holding that it amounted to an abuse of the provisions of the Bihar crime control law.The court imposed a cost of Rs2.2 lakh, or Rs 1.1 lakh each, as compensation to the two petitioners.The bench criticised the roles of the Nalanda SP and DM, describing the former as “acting as a post office” and the latter as “acting as a drastic power house” while declaring persons accused of minor offences as “antisocial”.The third case involved Girdhari Yadav, a resident of Katoria police station area in Banka district. The court found fault with an externment order dated Sept 8, 2025, passed by the Banka DM, under which Yadav had been directed to mark his daily attendance at Barahat police station, around 40km from his village.The court quashed the order and imposed a cost of Rs1.1 lakh on the state as compensation to Yadav.The bench directed the state govt to pay the compensation awarded to all four petitioners within a month and recover the amount from the officers found responsible.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: ‘May have to go back to cash’: Traders on UPI MDR
articles.summary: Delhi traders warn they may revert to cash after govt imposes 0.4% MDR on UPI payments above Rs 2,000; small merchants get exemption, MDR can’t be passed on.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: “We may have to go back to cash” – this is the refrain at Delhi’s markets after Centre introduced a 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.Traders and shopkeepers said they may stop accepting digital payments for larger transactions if they have to bear the additional cost.For businesses that have spent years shifting customers from cash to UPI, the move has come as a setback. They questioned why they should bear another transaction-related cost after paying GST and other business expenses. Some, they said, may now encourage customers to pay in cash.“We were already paying transaction charges and 18% GST. Now if govt charges us on UPI MDR, then we will promote cash. When govt came with the UPI payment method, we supported it. We are already grappling with issues like freezing of bank accounts and the imposition of restrictions due to complaints regarding cyber fraud. In such a climate, any additional increase in the cost of accepting digital payments is a cause for concern for small and medium-sized traders,” said Kamla Nagar Market Association president Nitin Gupta.“We have got used to digital payments. Sometimes, when we go to the market, we don’t even carry cash. It will be tough for us to go back to cash payments,” he added.Govt announced the charge Tuesday as part of a framework for large digital merchant payments, ending the zero-MDR regime that has been in place since Jan 2020.Traders and shop owners in several markets, including Kalkaji, Kamla Nagar, Khan Market, Laxmi Nagar and Sadar Bazar, said the decision has created confusion over who will bear the additional cost.They said even if the charge is not directly recovered from customers, it would add to the cost of doing business and could squeeze already limited margins.At Shree Shyam Jewellers in Kalkaji’s Block A, a shopkeeper said, “There is already so much confusion. After paying taxes, 18% GST and meeting so many other business expenses, an additional transaction charge is simply unacceptable. It will put another burden on us. We cannot keep absorbing costs,” he said.Brijesh Goel, chairperson of Chamber of Trade and Industry, said the move could encourage a shift towards cash transactions.“In the past six years, we have with great difficulty brought even the smallest of shopkeepers and street vendors onto UPI. Today, 90% of payments in Sadar Bazar, Chandni Chowk, Lajpat Nagar, Chawri Bazar, Kamla Nagar, Karol Bagh and Gandhi Nagar are through UPI. If MDR is imposed, it will be a setback to the Digital India mission,” he said.New Delhi Traders Association general secretary Amit Gupta said traders had no objection to digital payments but are opposed to the additional cost.“UPI was introduced to make digital payments easier for both traders and customers. If traders are now asked to bear an additional charge on transactions above Rs 2,000, many of them will prefer cash payment,” he said.Sadar Bazar Bari Market Traders Association president Paramjit Singh Pamma said the impact could be significant for businesses handling hundreds of large UPI transactions.“Profit margins are already limited, especially for small and medium-sized merchants. If merchants are charged for every large digital payment, it will directly impact their savings and profits,” Pamma said.The framework provides an exemption for small merchants earning up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes, with govt saying this covers 96% of merchant transactions.The MDR cannot be passed on to customers, while person-to-person UPI transfers remain outside the charge.Essential sectors such as railways, telecom and fuel will attract a flat Rs 5 fee per transaction, while capital market transactions will have a 0.02% rate.Petrol pump dealers, meanwhile, said they were waiting for clarity from the ministry of petroleum before deciding how to respond.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: 6 years on, gangster Vikas Dubey is officially dead
articles.summary: Kanpur Nagar Nigam issues Vikas Dubey death certificate six years after 2020 encounter, after High Court probe over wrong father’s name blocked insurance and property transfer.
articles.body: KANPUR: Kanpur Nagar Nigam issued the death certificate of gangster Vikas Dubey, the main accused in the Bikru case, on Sept 11, about six years after he was killed in a police encounter.Dubey died in Kanpur on July 10, 2020, but his death certificate could not be issued because his father’s name was incorrectly recorded in the panchnama and cremation slip. Instead of Ram Kumar Dubey, his father’s name was entered as Raj Kumar Dubey.His wife, Richa Dubey, approached several officials before filing a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court seeking the certificate. Following directions from the High Court, the health department investigated the matter.Chief medical officer Dr Hari Dutt Nemi visited the post-mortem house as part of the inquiry, after which the certificate was issued.Nagar Nigam sources said the certificate was sent by registered post to the Bikru address provided by the court. It was widely circulated on social media after reaching the village.Richa told the court that Dubey was not considered dead in the official records, preventing the nominee from receiving benefits under an insurance policy in his name. His property and land could also not be transferred to his heirs.On July 2, 2020, a police team went to Bikru village in Chaubepur police station area to arrest Dubey. Its vehicles were blocked with a JCB, and gunmen opened fire from rooftops as personnel approached his house.Eight policemen, including a circle officer, were killed. articles.title: Days after PM Modi’s school friend gets relief in land dispute, Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancels construction permission to BJP MLA’s company
articles.summary: Mira-Bhayander civic body cancels building permission for BJP MLA Narendra Mehta’s firm Seven Eleven amid land dispute; tehsildar rules for Asgarali Vohra.
articles.body: BHAYANDER: The Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation on Wednesday cancelled the construction permission granted to Seven Eleven company, days after BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land following the matter being taken up with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven and other respondents. The order is expected to clear the way for Vohra’s name to be entered in the land records for the property currently in the possession of Seven Eleven, which had fenced off the plot with metal sheets.Vohra had alleged that Mehta and Swayam Builders had illegally encroached on the land at Navghar in Bhayander. He had been pursuing the dispute for around 15 years.On September 8, Vohra approached PM Modi, whom he described as his childhood friend from B N School in Vadnagar in Gujarat, and sought his intervention in the dispute. Soon after, Mehta announced that he would relinquish possession of the property and withdraw a complaint filed against Vohra.On Wednesday, Mehta issued a statement denying that he or his company had cheated anyone. He said the disputed land had been sold to Vohra in 1989 by Renol Lobo and five others. Lobo and the others later sold the land to Swayam Builders in 2011, he said.Mehta further claimed that Seven Eleven had purchased the property through duly registered transactions from Joseph Fernandes and Mukesh Parekh. He said the company decided to return the land to Mukesh Parekh and Mervin Fernandes after a dispute arose over the property.The BJP MLA maintained that surrendering possession and cancelling the transaction was a decision taken to end the dispute and did not amount to an admission of wrongdoing.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Time-bound entry and exit plan for private vehicles at Pune airport awaited a year after announcement
articles.summary: Pune airport’s time-bound entry/exit plan for private vehicles remains unimplemented nearly a year on, amid congestion complaints; authorities say rollout is pending.
articles.body: PUNE: Almost a year after Pune airport authorities announced a time-bound entry and exit system for private vehicles, it is yet to be implemented.Pune airport director Santosh Dhoke told TOI that the plan was in its final stages, but officials were still working out the implementation mechanism to ensure passenger convenience. “Some discussions have been underway on how to effectively implement it so that flyers were not left in the lurch. Once we have found a proper way of implementation, it will start,” Dhoke said.He was talking on the sidelines of the announcement of the launch of ‘Yatri Seva Abhiyan’, a pan-India passenger-centric campaign from Sept 17 to Oct 10, 2026, organised by the Airports Authority of India (AAI).The delay in implementation has drawn criticism from frequent flyers. They said haphazardly parked vehicles outside the terminal obstructed the traffic and the airport shuttle movement, particularly during late evening and night hours.Ashish Sankule, a Ganeshkhind Road resident and regular flyer, said the airport needed to take a stricter approach towards vehicles blocking the arrival area. “Why was it taking so long for the airport authorities to implement this? It should have been simple – fine vehicles that block the pathway. There would always be people who protest, but the airport authorities needed to be strict,” he said.He said he had witnessed instances when shuttle buses operating between the airport and AeroMall struggled to move because of vehicles parked indiscriminately. “Those who follow the rules and park their vehicles at AeroMall end up finding it difficult to reach passengers waiting at the airport,” he said.Discussions on the time-bound system have been underway since last year. In Feb, airport authorities had said private vehicles would be given a maximum waiting window of 13-15 minutes to enter the airport, pick up passengers and exit. Vehicles exceeding the stipulated time were proposed to be penalised with hefty fines.Another frequent flyer and Koregaon Park resident, Shekhar Sinha, said implementation was necessary, but authorities also needed to address parking on the roads surrounding the airport.“Not just cabs, but private vehicles have been parked everywhere in the vicinity of the airport because people did not want to use AeroMall and pay parking fees. This was causing congestion on Airport Road and New Airport Road, but authorities did not seem to care,” he said.Sinha said airport authorities should implement the time-bound entry system immediately while coordinating with traffic police to tackle roadside parking. “If we have been talking about a ‘Yatri Seva Abhiyan’, these problems also need to be addressed,” he said.Dhoke said the transfer of 13 acres of defence land to the AAI, pending for nearly two years, was expected shortly. He said the required infrastructure has been completed for the Indian Air Force in lieu of the land. “The same was with the Defence Estate Office, and we should get it very soon. Once we get it, a plan would be drawn on what kind of expansion can be undertaken on the land as part of the masterplan,” Dhoke told TOI.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: 900m buffer zone earmarked in Gurgaon, but not even 9m gap between houses and IAF ammo depot
articles.summary: Gurgaon’s 900m buffer around an IAF ammo depot is densely encroached, with 15 illegal colonies and 5,000+ structures; SC questions officials’ collusion.
articles.body: GURGAON: The 900-metre restricted zone around Indian Air Force’s ammunition depot in old Gurgaon has been almost entirely built over, with multi-storey houses standing virtually flush against the facility’s boundary wall, leaving little to no buffer between habitation and a sensitive defence installation.Supreme Court on Tuesday criticised state officials for colluding with local land sharks to allow this encroachment. The depot was established in 1947.Fifteen illegal colonies have come up in the belt over the years, turning it into a dense urban pocket of kothis built cheek by jowl along narrow lanes.Residential buildings, PG accommodations, shops, schools, factories, cloud kitchens and commercial establishments now fill the zone. In several stretches, no open space separates the built-up area from the depot wall.Five- to seven-storey buildings have come up close to the installation, giving occupants elevated vantage points overlooking the depot — effectively erasing the physical buffer the restricted zone was meant to preserve.The affected pockets include Sheetla Colony, Rajiv Nagar, Sanjay Gram, Sukhrali Enclave, Ashok Vihar Phase 3, Om Vihar, Dharam Colony, Amanpura and Caterpuri, among others. The 900-metre zone covers roughly 2,325 acres.During Tuesday’s hearing, CJI Surya Kant said the no-go zone was earlier more than a kilometre and it gradually reduced to 900 metres, and even then, the illegal constructions were carried out right under the nose of the officials. “Are the encroachments not because of the collusion of govt officials with the land mafia,” he asked.Surveys and govt reports put the numbers differently. An MCG survey in 2017 identified 4,156 illegal structures within this belt. Officials estimate the number has since roughly doubled.Older govt data, including in the submissions made to the high court, had put total structures at 14,154, while a more recent MCG report flagged over 5,000 unauthorised structures and more than 190 ongoing construction sites in the zone.Punjab and Haryana high court had previously held that the 900-metre strip must remain free of urbanisation, and found that authorities allowed illegal construction to proliferate there. The court described the depot as a strategic installation where national interest could not be compromised.But govt action has repeatedly cut against this position. In 2015, Haryana filed an affidavit before the high court seeking to reduce the restricted zone from 900 to 300 metres.In 2016, the urban local bodies department approved temporary water connections for families in the 900-metre zone, citing the difficulty of removing thousands of residents.In 2017, authorities were directed to clear encroachments within a tighter 300-metre radius. A subsequent survey found 3,346 structures there, and the high court ordered their removal.MCG sealed several under-construction buildings last month, but a follow-up visit found many had been de-sealed and construction resumed. Hundreds of buildings are currently under construction in the zone.Residents describe a parallel civic ecosystem that has grown alongside the illegal settlement. A Sheetla Colony resident of about a decade alleged that local politicians and officials encouraged poor families to invest in construction there. “They help residents get voter cards and then use them as a vote bank during elections,” he said.A woman living in the area said residents have long been promised regularisation. “They help us get water and electricity connections. Roads have been built and sewerage laid,” she said.Another resident alleged that development tenders issued for adjoining areas are, in practice, executed inside the restricted zone: “Tenders are issued for development work in adjoining areas, but the actual work is carried out inside the 900-metre zone,” this person said.The issue has remained politically live. During the 2024 assembly campaign, Gurgaon MLA Mukesh Sharma listed resolving the zone’s problems among his priorities.In June 2026, Sharma met defence minister Rajnath Singh to seek the Centre’s intervention, citing the impact of the restrictions on civic works, property registrations and statutory approvals in the affected localities.A similar situation has played out near Faridabad Air Force Station in Dabua, where illegal construction within the restricted zone has been before Punjab and Haryana high court for over 15 years.The Centre notified a 100-metre restricted belt around the station in Jan 2010 under Works of Defence Act, prohibiting construction in the area. The matter reached the high court the same year through petitions seeking removal of illegal structures and action against officials responsible.In 2012, the court directed Faridabad Municipal Corporation to act against the illegal structures. By 2017, authorities estimated around 5,000 houses could be affected, and a 2018 survey identified 2,717 buildings within the 100-metre belt.Notices were issued to occupants, and authorities were directed to prevent further construction and transactions, but large populated colonies remain, with the issue still mired in legal and administrative hurdles.An area originally meant to stay free of urbanisation to protect a defence installation has become one of the city’s most densely populated pockets — serviced, in part, by the same civic machinery meant to keep it clear.With construction still underway, the unresolved question is not how the colonies came up, but how thousands of structures have been allowed to remain, expand and receive civic infrastructure inside a decades-old security zone.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: FATO OU FAKE: Entrevistas com candidados ao governo do RJ no RJ1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos), Douglas Ruas (PL) e Eduardo Paes (PSD) foram sabatinados nesta semana.
articles.summary: Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos), Douglas Ruas (PL) e Eduardo Paes (PSD) foram sabatinados nesta semana.
articles.body:
Garotinho, Douglas Ruas e Eduardo Paes durante entrevista ao RJ1 — Foto: Reprodução

Os candidatos ao governo do Rio de Janeiro Anthony Garotinho ( Republicanos ), Douglas Ruas ( PL ) e Eduardo Paes ( PSD ) foram entrevistados pelo RJ1 nesta semana. Conduzidas pelos jornalistas Mariana Gross e Edimilson Ávila, as conversas sobre os principais temas do estado foram exibidas ao vivo no telejornal.

O público pôde acompanhar a transmissão pela TV Globo e pelo g1 , que depois disponibilizou a íntegra, assim como o Globoplay . Foram convidados os dois candidatos mais bem colocados na pesquisa de intenção de voto divulgada pelo Datafolha em 11 de setembro .

Segunda-feira (14) - Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos) – leia mais sobre a sabatina

Terça-feira (15) - Douglas Ruas (PL) – leia mais sobre a sabatina

Quarta-feira (16) - Eduardo Paes (PSD) – leia mais sobre a sabatina

A equipe do Fato ou Fake checou as principais declarações dos candidatos. Leia:

"No Alemão, o chefe do Comando Vermelho fala com um cara de Cabedelo, na Paraíba. Os bandidos de fora estão vindo para o Rio de Janeiro, sendo treinados e voltando para os seus estados."

Operações da Polícia Federal e do Ministério Público da Paraíba já tiveram como principal alvo de investigação o Comando Vermelho e sua atuação em Cabedelo, cidade de 60 mil habitantes.

Segundo as apurações, a facção se infiltrou em pontos estratégicos da prefeitura do município.

A investigação, segundo uma reportagem exibida em maio pelo Fantástico , cita que Flávio de Lima Monteiro, o Fatoka, estava foragido em maio deste ano no Complexo do Alemão.

Fatoka é apontado como criador da Tropa do Amigão, braço do Comando Vermelho no Nordeste.

A presença de traficantes de outros estados no Alemão e outras comunidades do Rio já foi tema de diversas reportagens no g1 e no Fantástico .

Os treinamentos de criminosos são uma realidade no Rio de Janeiro. Em 2023, imagens de um treinamento de guerrilha no Complexo da Maré foram divulgadas pelo próprio Fantástico .

"Cabe recurso [da condenação por improbidade]."

Durante entrevista, a apresentadora Mariana Gross citou três vezes que a condenação de Garotinho por improbidade administrativa de 2018 é definitiva e que não cabe mais recurso. Garotinho, no entanto, rebateu duas vezes: "Cabe recurso".

Isso não é verdade. A condenação por improbidade administrativa transitou em julgado no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), ou seja, tornou-se definitiva, sem possibilidade de recurso.

É possível, porém, questionar os efeitos da condenação, como multa e indenização por danos, por meio de instrumentos jurídicos próprios.

No caso, a defesa de Garotinho ajuizou em agosto de 2026 uma ação rescisória para tentar desconstituir esses efeitos. O pedido de liminar nessa ação foi negado , mas essa decisão ainda pode ser contestada por recurso. Isso, no entanto, não significa que ainda seja possível recorrer da condenação original.

Procurada pelo Fato ou Fake , a assessoria de imprensa Garotinho reconheceu que não cabe mais recurso na ação que resultou na condenação, mas afirmou que ainda existem recursos e medidas judiciais para discutir os efeitos da decisão.

Também cabe recurso, junto ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), sobre a decisão do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral que indeferiu a candidatura de Garotinho devido a essa condenação transitada em julgado.

"O relatório diz que elas [milícias] cresceram no período do governo de Sérgio Cabral. No meu período, existia uma milícia forte no Rio de Janeiro: a de Rio das Pedras, que era comandada pelo Nadinho. [...] Ela começa a se articular no ano 2000. Ela ganha força a partir do governo de Sérgio Cabral."

Selo Não é Bem Assim (Horizontal) — Foto: g1

Em termos cronológicos, o relatório da CPI das Milícias afirmou que os grupos de milicianos tinham um objetivo "legítimo" de expulsar traficantes de determinadas localidades oito anos antes do início da comissão, ou seja, em 2000, exatamente durante o governo de Garotinho.

Em outro trecho, o relatório diz que as milícias tiveram um "vertiginoso aumento" a partir de 2004, ano em que a governadora do Rio de Janeiro era Rosinha Garotinho, esposa do ex-governador e atual candidato.

O trecho exato diz: "A expressão milícias se incorporou ao vocabulário da segurança pública no Estado do Rio e começou a ser usada frequentemente por órgãos de imprensa quando as mesmas tiveram vertiginoso aumento, a partir de 2004".

Outro trecho do relatório final da CPI das milícias aponta que os ataques de dezembro de 2006 , que atingiram ônibus, delegacias e postos da Polícia Militar do Rio, também ajudaram a consolidar o uso do termo "milícia". Os atentados, segundo o texto, seriam uma "ação de represália de facções de narcotraficantes à propagação de milícias na cidade".

O governo de Sérgio Cabral só começou em janeiro de 2007. A partir daí, houve acontecimentos relevantes relacionados à atuação dos grupos criminosos, como as prisões do deputado estadual Natalino e do vereador Jerominho, em 2008.

"Você lembra, que você era repórter, eu baixei as tarifas [de ônibus intermunicipal] da outra vez, baixei 15%."

Em 1999, o então governador Anthony Garotinho, por meio do Decreto estadual nº 25.194, de 12 de fevereiro de 1999, reduziu em 15% as tarifas praticadas pelas empresas permissionárias de transporte urbano e intermunicipal.

O Tribunal de Justiça do RJ, no entanto, declarou a nulidade dos decretos, o que levou ao ajuizamento de mais de 100 ações das empresas de ônibus para reaver seus prejuízos.

"Quem me escolheu para ser candidato a governador foi o presidente Bolsonaro."

Uma reportagem publicada em fevereiro pelo jornal "O Globo" relatou que, segundo aliados de Jair Bolsonaro, o ex-presidente defendeu que o PL lançasse o então deputado estadual licenciado e secretário estadual de Cidades, Douglas Ruas, como candidato ao governo do Rio.

Nas conversas, Bolsonaro avaliou que Ruas poderia representar o campo bolsonarista na disputa.

No mesmo mês, o PL anunciou oficialmente a pré-candidatura de Ruas ao governo do estado. O anúncio foi feito pelo senador e pré-candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ).

"Aquela operação [Alemão], o estado [RJ] perdeu uma grande oportunidade numa única ação com mais de 2,4 mil policiais que foram recebidos por tiros de fuzil, drones atirando granada, tiro de .50, lograram êxito em retirar de circulação mais de 200 marginais que impõem um verdadeiro terror à população de bem que mora naquelas comunidades."

Na entrevista, Douglas Ruas falou em "200 marginais". O número corresponde à soma aproximada dos 117 suspeitos mortos e das 123 pessoas presas ou apreendidas na operação de 28 de outubro de 2025, realizada nos complexos do Alemão e da Penha.

As autoridades, no entanto, não confirmaram que todos os mortos e presos eram criminosos, com antecedentes ou mandados de prisão em aberto.

As informações divulgadas não comprovam individualmente que todos os mortos na operação estavam armados, portavam fuzis ou atiraram contra os agentes. A própria Polícia Civil informou que parte deles não tinha histórico criminal, e as circunstâncias das mortes continuaram sujeitas à perícia e à investigação.

De acordo com o relatório do Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ), a megaoperação deixou 121 mortos (quatro policiais e 117 suspeitos). O MP apontou que 20 mortos não tinham qualquer envolvimento com o crime. O relatório também registrou civis atingidos por balas perdidas, entre eles um morador de rua, Fernando Vinicius Lopes, que morreu, e uma mulher ferida em uma academia.

Ao todo, 113 pessoas foram presas, e dez adolescentes foram apreendidos. A própria Secretaria de Polícia Civil divulgou que, dos 113 adultos presos, apenas 54 tinham anotações criminais. Ou seja, mais da metade não tinha registro anterior de antecedentes no sistema.

Entre os 117 mortos, segundo levantamento da Polícia Civil, ao menos 97 tinham histórico criminal, 59 tinham mandados de prisão pendentes e 17 não apresentavam histórico criminal.

Com relação a 12 desses 17 casos, o governo afirmou ter encontrado, em redes sociais, indício de participação dessas pessoas no tráfico. Duas identificações ou perícias ainda estavam inconclusivas no levantamento divulgado.

Em novembro de 2025, o policial civil Rodrigo Vasconcellos Nascimento, lotado na 39ª DP (Pavuna), morreu após 20 dias internado. Rodrigo foi alvo de disparos de traficantes no alto da Serra da Misericórdia naquele dia 28 de outubro. Com a morte do agente, subiu para cinco o número de policiais mortos na operação.

O Fato ou Fake procurou a assessoria de Douglas Ruas para saber em que dados ele se baseou ao citar os "200 marginais" retirados de circulação. A resposta cita que o candidato se referiu aos "100 criminosos que foram presos e aos 117 que morreram em confronto com a polícia". A nota, no entanto, não informou qual documento foi usado como referência para a declaração feita na entrevista desta quarta.

"Além disso, teve uma significativa melhora na merenda escolar que recentemente ganhou um prêmio nacional, o melhor projeto nutricional do Brasil."

Segundo uma publicação de 14 de julho no site oficial da Prefeitura de São Gonçalo, a Escola Estadual Municipalizada Itaitindiba, no bairro de Santa Izabel, ganhou um prêmio como uma das 20 unidades selecionadas no país, concedido em janeiro de 2026.

O projeto participante foi o “Feirinha na escola: sabores da agricultura”, que incentiva a agricultura familiar do município.

O prêmio faz parte da 7ª edição da Jornada de Educação Alimentar e Nutricional (EAN). A escola foi escolhida no núcleo de atividades número 3, cujo tema era "Agricultores(as) familiares como protagonistas da ação de EAN". A iniciativa, no entanto, não prevê um prêmio específico para o “melhor projeto nutricional” do Brasil .

A jornada é uma iniciativa do Fundo Nacional de Desenvolvimento da Educação (FNDE) voltada para escolas públicas da Educação Básica atendidas pelo Programa Nacional de Alimentação Escolar (PNAE), do governo federal. O prêmio é uma iniciativa para fortalecer e dar visibilidade às ações de educação alimentar e nutricional no ambiente escolar em todo o país.

"Quando o prefeito [Capitão Nelson] assumiu a cidade de São Gonçalo, a cidade estava uma terra arrasada. A rede pública municipal tinha apenas 30 e poucos mil alunos, 34 mil alunos [...]. Hoje, já dobrou o número de alunos, já contam com mais de 60 mil."

Capitão Nelson (PL), pai de Douglas Ruas, foi eleito prefeito de São Gonçalo em 2020, e reeleito em 2024.

Consultada pelo Fato ou Fake , a assessoria de imprensa da prefeitura do município afirmou que havia 35 mil alunos matriculados na rede municipal em 2021.

Atualmente, são 60 mil estudantes, contabilizando os Centros Especializados, como os Centros de Referência Municipal do Autista, Centro de Inclusão e Centro Interescolar Ulysses Guimarães (CIUG).

"Eu não participei do projeto Cidade Integrada. Existiu a Secretaria da Cidade em uma configuração anterior, ela foi extinta. Essa foi na primeira gestão do governador Cláudio Castro, da qual eu não participei. Tinha uma Secretaria das Cidades, que posteriormente ela foi extinta. Essa, sim, participou do Cidade Integrada. Em 2023, foi criada uma nova secretaria, Secretaria das Cidades, com a mesma nomenclatura, mas ela não participou do programa Cidade Integrada em relação à questão da Segurança Pública."

Em janeiro de 2022, o Decreto nº 47928 criou o Cidade Integrada e inclui a Secretaria de Estado das Cidades (Secid) no núcleo de governança estratégica do programa. Cláudio Castro já era governador do Rio de Janeiro desde 2021, após a cassação de Wilson Witzel .

No texto, a Secid é listada como integrante do núcleo "tático-operacional" do programa.

Em 1° de janeiro de 2023, o Decreto nº 48.031 extinguiu a Secretaria de Estado de Infraestrutura e Obras e a Secretaria de Estado das Cidades.

Nove dias depois, o Decreto 48.314 criou, sem aumento de despesa, a estrutura organizacional da Secretaria de Estado de Infraestrutura e Cidades, que fundiu as duas secretarias que haviam sido extintas em 1° de janeiro.

Em 26 de setembro de 2023, o Decreto 48.707 determinou a mudança no nome da pasta, que passou a se chamar Secretaria de Estado de Infraestrutura e Obras Públicas (Seiop).

No mesmo decreto, o governador anunciou, também sem aumentar despesas, a criação da Secretaria de Estado das Cidades (Secid), e Douglas Ruas foi nomeado secretário. Cargos comissionados da Seiop foram transferidos para a Secid.

Em outubro de 2023, o Decreto 48.780 transferiu os projetos executivos da Seiop, inclusive o Cidade Integrada, à Secid.

Em 16 de novembro de 2023, o Decreto 48.707, após aprovação da Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Alerj), foi transformado em lei e publicado no Diário Oficial. A Lei nº 10.181 determinou uma reforma administrativa que criou oficialmente a Secid, o mesmo nome utilizado na criação do programa Cidade Integrada em 2022. Nenhum dos decretos citados foi revogado posteriormente.

A Secretaria de Cidades seguiu integrando o projeto Cidade Integrada, que existe até hoje.

"O Chiquinho Brazão foi uma indicação do Republicanos. Não havia sequer nenhuma suspeita contra ele. E tem que lembrar que o assassinato da Marielle tinha acontecido 6 meses antes e nunca se levantou nenhuma suspeita contra ele e a própria suspeita contra o irmão dele já tinha meio que sido apagada. [...] Quando surge a primeira notícia de possibilidade de envolvimento dele, eu demito ele imediatamente. Tanto que ele é preso meses depois."

Chiquinho Brazão foi indicado pelo Republicanos para assumir a Secretaria Especial de Ação Comunitária da Prefeitura do Rio. A nomeação ocorreu em 3 de outubro de 2023, em meio à articulação política entre o prefeito Eduardo Paes e o partido para as eleições municipais de 2024.

A escolha aconteceu em um momento em que novas suspeitas sobre Domingos Brazão, irmão de Chiquinho, haviam voltado ao centro das investigações sobre a morte de Marielle Franco. O avanço das suspeitas e o envio do caso ao Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ) foram revelados pelo colunista do jornal "O Globo" Bernardo Mello Franco .

O ex-policial militar Ronnie Lessa, condenado por executar Marielle e Anderson Gomes, apontou Domingos Brazão como um dos mandantes do crime em seu acordo de delação premiada.

A prisão de Chiquinho Brazão, Domingos Brazão e Rivaldo Barbosa , apontados pela investigação como envolvidos no caso, ocorreu em 24 de março de 2024.

Chiquinho deixou a Secretaria Especial de Ação Comunitária em 1º de fevereiro de 2024, quando foi exonerado pela Prefeitura do Rio, na gestão de Eduardo Paes.

"Sabe como é que pegaram os assassinos da Marielle? Usando as câmeras do Centro de Operações [...] Se desvendou, por exemplo, o assassinato da Marielle através do Centro de Operações da Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro."

Imagens de câmeras da Prefeitura do Rio ajudaram a Polícia Civil a identificar o carro usado pelos assassinos de Marielle Franco, Élcio Queiroz e Ronnie Lessa. O Cobalt prata seguia o carro do motorista de Marielle, Anderson Gomes , que também foi morto no ataque.

A partir das imagens, a Polícia Civil passou a monitorar o itinerário do veículo usado no crime.

No entanto, pelo menos cinco câmeras que mostravam o trajeto de Marielle antes do crime estavam desligadas . O percurso era de aproximadamente três quilômetros.

As investigações apontam que Lessa e Élcio Queiroz foram presos a partir de um conjunto de provas , que incluiu, além das imagens, uma denúncia anônima ligando ambos diretamente ao crime, a quebra de sigilo telemático e o cruzamento de dados de localização dos condenados pelas mortes de Marielle e Anderson.

A quebra do sigilo do telefone de Ronnie Lessa possibilitou que a polícia identificasse Élcio como motorista do carro no dia do crime.

"A passagem mais cara do estado do Rio de Janeiro é de São Gonçalo, que aumentou para R$ 5,40 em novembro do ano passado."

Em Niterói, o passageiro que utiliza o Bilhete Único Niterói, subsidiado pela Prefeitura, paga R$ 4,45. Para quem paga em dinheiro ou não tem direito ao benefício, a tarifa é de R$ 5,60, também superior à de São Gonçalo.

Além disso, a tarifa dos ônibus municipais de São Gonçalo foi reajustada para R$ 5,55 em novembro de 2025, e não para R$ 5,40, como afirmou Paes.

"Nós tivemos quatro secretários do Cláudio Castro presos por ligações com o crime. Um ia ser candidato a governador. Nós temos, neste momento, dois secretários do Cláudio Castro presos, o Rodrigo Bacellar, três vezes preso por ligações com o Comando Vermelho, e o tal do Carracena, acho que é esse o nome, que nesta semana o TRF tornou réu de novo com o TH Joias."

Allan Turnowski, ex-secretário estadual de Polícia Civil, foi preso em 2022. O Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ) o denunciou sob acusação de integrar uma organização criminosa ligada ao jogo do bicho e de atuar em favor de contraventores. Atualmente, responde em liberdade.

Raphael Montenegro, então secretário estadual de Administração Penitenciária, foi preso em 2021. A investigação apontava suspeitas de negociação de vantagens com integrantes do Comando Vermelho.

Alessandro Pitombeira Carracena ocupou as secretarias estaduais de Esporte e Lazer e de Defesa do Consumidor e havia sido secretário municipal de Ordem Pública durante a gestão Marcelo Crivella. Está preso desde setembro de 2025. Segundo investigação da Polícia Federal (PF), ele integraria o núcleo político de uma organização ligada ao Comando Vermelho. Carracena e outros acusados no caso agora são réus na Justiça.

Rodrigo Bacellar, ex-presidente da Assembleia Legistlativa do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) que foi secretário estadual de Governo de Castro, também foi preso. Em março de 2026, o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) voltou a decretar sua prisão preventiva por suspeitas de vazamento de informações e obstrução de investigações relacionadas a organizações criminosas.

articles.title: Mulher desaparecida em Bauru: família busca Marciene há 10 dias | G1
articles.standfirst: Marciene Pereira da Silva Soares, de 50 anos, foi vista pela última vez na manhã de 4 de setembro após deixar a filha na escola. Câmeras de segurança registraram a mulher caminhando pelo bairro.
articles.summary: A mulher desaparecida em Bauru, Marciene Pereira da Silva Soares, foi vista pela última vez após deixar a filha na escola e o caso é investigado pela Polícia Civil.
articles.body:
A mãe da dona de casa Marciene Pereira da Silva Soares, desaparecida há mais de 10 dias em Bauru (SP) após deixar uma das filhas na escola, diz que a filha jamais sumiu sem dar notícias.

Em entrevista ao g1 , Marlene Pereira da Silva, de 71 anos, ressaltou que Marciene sempre foi responsável por levar e buscar as crianças na escola e que nunca agiu dessa forma antes.

"Nunca saiu sem avisar, de jeito nenhum. É um desespero, não tenho como descrever. A gente acorda de noite, não consegue dormir... o único jeito é esperar e ter muita fé em Deus", desabafou Marlene.

Marciene Pereira da Silva Soares, de 50 anos, saiu para caminhar em Bauru (SP) e não voltou mais — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda segundo Marlene, as filhas de Marciene, de 8 e 13 anos, perguntam diariamente pelo paradeiro da mãe. De acordo com a idosa, a caçula é quem mais demonstra sofrimento com a ausência materna.

"A pequenininha é a que mais fala 'eu quero que a minha mãe volte pra casa'", conta.

Marciene saiu de casa por volta das 7h do dia 4 de setembro acompanhada das filhas, de 8 e 13 anos, segundo o boletim de ocorrência registrado pelo marido.

Ela levou uma das crianças para a escola e deixou a outra na casa da mãe, no Núcleo Habitacional José Regino. Na ocasião, disse à mãe que iria caminhar e passar no mercado. Desde então, não foi mais vista.

Conforme o boletim de ocorrência, Marciene saiu sem o celular, a mãe explicou que ela tinha o hábito de não levar o aparelho quando saía para caminhar ou de deixá-lo com a filha mais velha. Ela não tem histórico de desaparecimentos anteriores.

Imagens de câmeras de segurança obtidas pela família mostram a dona de casa caminhando pela calçada de uma rua do bairro com as mesmas roupas descritas no boletim de ocorrência. (Assista ao vídeo no início da reportagem).

Dona de casa desaparece após deixar filha na escola em Bauru — Foto: Câmera de segurança

De acordo com o registro policial, Marciene tem aproximadamente 1,70 m de altura, é magra e possui cabelos curtos castanhos. No dia do desaparecimento, ela usava shorts preto, camiseta branca, boné e carregava uma mochila rosa.

Informações sobre o paradeiro da dona de casa podem ser repassadas anonimamente à polícia pelos telefones 190, 197 ou pelo Disque Denúncia 181.

articles.title: Temporal com granizo provoca estragos no Vale do Aço | G1
articles.standfirst: Tempestade atingiu Ipatinga, Timóteo, Coronel Fabriciano e Santana do Paraíso na noite de quarta-feira. Houve alagamentos, queda de árvores, desabamento de galpão e interrupções no fornecimento de energia e água.
articles.summary: Tempestade atingiu Ipatinga, Timóteo, Coronel Fabriciano e Santana do Paraíso na noite de quarta-feira (16).
articles.body:
Um temporal acompanhado de granizo atingiu cidades do Vale do Aço na noite desta quarta-feira (16) e provocou uma série de transtornos na região. Ipatinga , Timóteo , Coronel Fabriciano e Santana do Paraíso registraram ocorrências relacionadas à chuva forte e aos ventos intensos, como alagamentos, queda de árvores, destelhamentos e interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica.

Os impactos também afetaram serviços essenciais. Em razão da falta de energia registrada após a tempestade, a Copasa informou que o abastecimento de água poderá apresentar intermitências em municípios da região. Equipes das prefeituras, da Defesa Civil, do Corpo de Bombeiros, da Cemig e da concessionária de abastecimento foram mobilizadas para atender às ocorrências.

Ipatinga registra queda de árvores, falta de energia e interdição na BR-381

Bairro Ferroviários, Ipatinga — Foto: Cristiane Rodrigues/g1

Em Ipatinga, a prefeitura informou que equipes da Defesa Civil, Trânsito, Serviços Urbanos, Corpo de Bombeiros e Cemig saíram às ruas para atender chamados e monitorar a situação em diferentes pontos da cidade.

Segundo o município, durante cerca de uma hora de tempestade foram registrados 38,8 milímetros de chuva e rajadas de vento de 76,2 quilômetros por hora. Houve pontos de alagamento e registros de quedas de árvores e postes. De acordo com a Defesa Civil, até o momento não havia registro de ocorrências graves ou vítimas.

O trecho mais crítico identificado pelas equipes fica na BR-381, na altura do km 250, no sentido Governador Valadares , que foi obstruído pela queda de árvores e postes. Os trabalhos se concentraram na liberação da via e na sinalização do local.

A Copasa informou que, devido à interrupção de energia elétrica, o abastecimento de água na cidade poderá apresentar intermitências nesta quinta-feira (17). A previsão é de que o fornecimento seja normalizado gradativamente após o restabelecimento da energia. A companhia destaca que imóveis com caixas d'água podem não sofrer impactos.

Em razão dos transtornos provocados pela tempestade, quatro escolas da rede municipal não tiveram aulas no período da manhã desta quinta-feira : Escola Municipal Padre Bertollo, Escola Municipal Pato Donald, Escola Municipal Infantil 07 de Outubro e Escola Municipal Carlos Drummond de Andrade. As demais unidades funcionaram normalmente.

Em nota, o prefeito Gustavo Nunes (PL) afirmou que a falta de energia é generalizada no Vale do Aço e explicou que a tempestade atingiu primeiro Timóteo e Coronel Fabriciano. Segundo ele, a prioridade das equipes é a desobstrução das vias de acesso a hospitais, unidades de saúde e corredores viários para possibilitar o deslocamento dos técnicos da Cemig.

Timóteo tem alagamentos, queda de árvores e problemas no abastecimento de água

Pedras de granizo em Timóteo — Foto: Redes sociais

Em Timóteo, uma das áreas mais afetadas foi a Regional Leste, especialmente nos bairros Jardim Vitória e Recanto Verde. Algumas vias ficaram tomadas pela enxurrada, dificultando a passagem de veículos e pedestres.

Também houve registros de queda de árvores na região do Centro Norte e no bairro Serenata. O fornecimento de energia elétrica foi afetado em diversos pontos da cidade. A prefeitura informou que realiza um levantamento para avaliar os impactos provocados pela chuva.

A Copasa informou que a falta de energia poderá causar intermitências no abastecimento de água em diversos bairros do município. A previsão é que o fornecimento seja normalizado gradativamente após o restabelecimento da energia elétrica.

Os bairros que podem ser afetados são Alegre, Alvorada, Ana Malaquias, Ana Moura, Ana Rita, Bela Vista, Bromélias, Centro, Centro Sul, Colinas, Coqueiro, Cruzeirinho, Eldorado, Funcionários, Garapa, Jardim Primavera, João XXIII, John Kennedy, Nossa Senhora das Graças, Nova Esperança, Novo Horizonte, Novo Tempo, Núcleo Industrial, Olaria, Primavera, Quitandinha, Santa Cecília, Santa Maria, Santa Terezinha, São Cristóvão, São José, Serenata, Timirim, Timotinho, Vale Verde e Vila dos Técnicos. A companhia ressalta que imóveis com caixas d'água podem não sofrer impactos.

Em Coronel Fabriciano, vento derruba galpão e afeta abastecimento

Ventania forte derrubou um galpão e interditou avenida em Coronel Fabriciano — Foto: Redes sociais

Em Coronel Fabriciano, a força do vento provocou o desabamento de um galpão no bairro Santa Terezinha. Não foram divulgadas informações sobre feridos.

A cidade também registrou falta de energia elétrica em diversos pontos. Em razão da situação, a Copasa informou que o abastecimento de água poderá apresentar intermitências ao longo desta quinta-feira (17).

Segundo a companhia, a normalização do serviço ocorrerá gradativamente após o restabelecimento da energia elétrica pela concessionária responsável. A empresa reforçou que imóveis com reservatórios de água podem não sentir os efeitos da interrupção.

Santana do Paraíso registra poucos impactos, segundo prefeitura

Santana do Paraíso também foi atingida pela tempestade, mas, segundo a prefeitura, os impactos foram menores em comparação com outros municípios da região.

De acordo com o prefeito Bruno Morato (Avante), o resultado está relacionado a ações preventivas realizadas nos últimos anos, como a desobstrução periódica de bocas de lobo, limpeza do sistema de drenagem urbana, identificação de árvores com risco de queda e substituição de espécies consideradas mais vulneráveis.

O prefeito destacou ainda que equipes também atuam na limpeza e desobstrução de córregos e que o município passou a integrar o Conclima, consórcio nacional voltado à prevenção de desastres climáticos e à captação de recursos para enfrentamento de eventos extremos.

Apesar dos menores impactos registrados, a cidade também teve reflexos da falta de energia. A Copasa informou que alguns bairros poderão apresentar intermitências no abastecimento de água nesta quinta-feira (17).

Os bairros afetados são Alto Santana, Centro, Chácaras Paraíso, Josefino Anício, Oliveira, Residencial Paraíso, São Francisco, São José, Vale do Paraíso e Veraneio. Segundo a companhia, a normalização do abastecimento ocorrerá gradativamente após o restabelecimento da energia elétrica. Imóveis que possuem caixas d'água podem não sofrer impactos.

As autoridades orientam a população a evitar áreas de risco, não atravessar vias alagadas e manter distância de árvores, postes e redes elétricas. Em casos de emergência, a Defesa Civil pode ser acionada pelo telefone 199 e o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193.

articles.title: Vídeos da influenciadora chegam a ter 5,2 milhões de visualizações | G1
articles.standfirst: Eliziane Ferreira tem mais de três milhões de seguidores e publica vídeos em parceria com outros influenciadores do Tocantins.
articles.summary: Eliziane Ferreira tem mais de três milhões de seguidores e publica vídeos em parceria com outros influenciadores do Tocantins.
articles.body:
Eliziane Ferreira, que interpreta a personagem 'Bebinha Arueira', viralizou nas redes sociais com vídeos de brincadeiras e piadas. Uma das publicações que mais chamou atenção dos internautas foi o reencontro de Eliziane com a família, que mora na Bahia (veja acima).

A influenciadora teve um bar durante 10 anos, e foi com as vivências que teve no local, que decidiu criar a personagem. "Observava os gestos e as mulheres sempre andavam com copo na mão, com os vestidos. E bem alegres, igual a Bebinha".

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Desde que a personagem começou a chamar atenção nas redes sociais, a influenciadora já viralizou com o vídeo falando sobre a saudade que tem dos filhos, que tem 2,4 milhões de visualizações. O encontro com o cantor Gusttavo Lima também viralizou e conta com mais de 5 milhões de visualizações, além de vídeos em parceria com outros influenciadores que possuem milhões de acessos.

Eliziane Ferreira Cruz gravava relato sobre a saudade de casa quando foi surpreendida pelo marido e pela filha mais nova — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Eliziane Ferreira Cruz

Natural de Itaguaçu da Bahia, Eliziane reside temporariamente no Tocantins para cumprir uma agenda de gravações com o projeto Bar do Arueira e parcerias com criadores de conteúdo locais. O humor irreverente fez a artista alcançar 3,2 milhões de seguidores no Instagram e aproximadamente 582 mil no TikTok, além de ganhar projeção nacional após participar do reality show Rancho do Maia, comandado por Carlinhos Maia.

Na última semana, a humorista publicou um agradecimento especial após registrar o marco de 1 bilhão de acessos em 30 dias. Fora das esquetes de comédia, Eliziane sempre enfatizou que o trabalho longe de casa tem como objetivo principal garantir melhores condições e estabilidade para a família que permaneceu na Bahia.

articles.title: DUSU elections: ABVP, NSUI trade allegations of attacks and intimidation ahead of polls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With Delhi University set to vote for its students’ union on September 18, the ABVP and National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) have trade.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With Delhi University set to vote for its students’ union on September 18, the ABVP and National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) have traded allegations of attacks and intimidation involving their members and candidates, with both student organisations demanding police action.In a press statement, the ABVP alleged that NSUI workers entered the residence of its members at Hari Mandir in Delhi and attacked them while they were holding a meeting.It said women student members were also present at the residence when the alleged incident took place.The ABVP alleged that several individuals fled the spot after the alleged attack, while one person was apprehended by its members and handed over to the police. It further claimed that the apprehended person admitted to being part of NSUI’s social media cadre.ABVP Delhi State secretary Sarthak Sharma said, "NSUI must explain why its workers reached the residence of ABVP members and attacked them despite women student activists being present there. ABVP members were holding a peaceful meeting and had not provoked anyone. One person who was fleeing after the attack was apprehended and handed over to the police. ABVP did not take the law into its own hands; instead, we handed the individual over to the police.""The apprehended person has admitted to being part of NSUI's social media cadre. Congress-IYC-NSUI must explain why its social media cadre was involved in an attack on the residence of ABVP members? Students of Delhi University can clearly see the difference between democratic student engagement and the use of violence. ABVP members are continuously engaging with students peacefully, while people associated with Congress-IYC-NSUI are allegedly resorting to violence," he alleged.Sharma further noted, "The Congress leadership must clarify its political accountability for the activities of its youth and student organisations. ABVP will not be intimidated by violence or pressure. We demand an impartial police investigation and strict legal action against all those involved, along with adequate measures to ensure the safety of students. The facts of the incident can also be verified from the local police."The NSUI, meanwhile, alleged that ABVP workers attacked the residences of its DUSU candidates Vijay Shankar Meena and Gopal Choudhary. It alleged that nearly 200 ABVP workers were involved in targeting and intimidating its candidates.NSUI Media Incharge Ravi Pandey said, "This is a desperate attempt to create fear and violence just before the DUSU elections. We demand immediate intervention and strict action by the Delhi Police to ensure the safety of our candidates and students. Such hooliganism cannot be allowed in a democratic student election.""ABVP knows that students are ready for change. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil on Thursday called off his 20-day-old hunger strike and gave the Maharashtra government three months to consider his demands, news agency PTI reported.The decision came after Jarange addressed a large gathering at Patoda in Beed district around 2 am, raising concerns about his worsening physical condition and the possibility of abandoning his planned march to Mumbai.Jarange, who had entered the day 18 of his fast at the time of the address, said he was too physically exhausted to continue a long journey with thousands of supporters travelling behind him.He asked Maratha community members not to follow his vehicle after he left Patoda. Instead, he urged them to meet him directly at Khopoli. He warned that if the convoy continued, he might stop the journey and resume his sit-in protest in Patoda or return to Antarwali Sarati.Despite reaching the venue at around 1.30 am, Jarange found thousands of people, including women, waiting to hear him speak.Addressing the gathering, he said he could barely move his limbs after stopping IV fluids on September 12."Fighting for the children of my community has taken a toll on my body, but I have taken on the government for you. The government wants me to surrender, but should I abandon our demand? My community is greater than any government - it is my father. My community holds the power to bring down any government and install a new one," he asserted.Jarange said the movement had made progress after 58 lakh archival records, known as nondi, were uncovered. He claimed these records could help nearly 2.5 crore members of the Maratha community access reservation benefits.He said the immediate demand was for the Maharashtra government to issue an official gazette recognising the relevant records.The activist also criticised chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, claiming he had countered the government's political moves and that all the documented records had been secured on pen drives. He further accused Fadnavis of "plotting against his life".Responding to the government's argument about fruit orchard owners in Western Maharashtra, Jarange questioned why OBC communities that also own orchards should not receive reservation benefits."The government claims Western Maharashtra has fruit orchards, but don't OBC communities own orchards too? Why do they have a reservation then?"Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike. He appealed to supporters to avoid following his vehicle and said he would prefer to travel directly to Mumbai from Patoda after speaking to the police, if his health allowed.He also spoke about his family, saying he had asked them to live with self-respect and told his son to remain courageous if he died for the community."I have told my family to live with self-respect. I told my son to step up courageously if I give my life for the community. Let one life be sacrificed for the cause, but never let the dignity of our caste be lowered," he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: AT&T CEO John Stankey, as part of our company's culture we have a principle for all meetings: Do not walk into a meeting without ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: AT&T CEO John Stankey has laid out a clear cultural principle for his company that employees should never walk into a meeting unprepared. Accordin.
articles.body: AT&T CEO John Stankey has laid out a clear cultural principle for his company that employees should never walk into a meeting unprepared. According to a report by Fortune, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon, hosted by LinkedIN, Stankey emphasised that success requires discourse, data-driven perspectives, and the courage to speak up. Stankey said one of AT&T’s guiding principles is that employees must come to meetings ready to contribute. “Don’t walk in there and just be an observer,” he explained. “When you have a point of view, it shouldn’t just be some uninformed opinion. It should be a point of view that’s built on facts, information, and data. I crave that.”He added that if participants aren’t willing to share constructive insights, it may mean the wrong people are in the room. The approach is designed to avoid groupthink and ensure meetings are productive rather than ceremonial.JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon’s perspectiveJamie Dimon echoed Stankey’s sentiment, noting that leaders must create environments where employees feel comfortable disagreeing or raising uncomfortable issues. “I am never upset when someone says I’m wrong about something,” Dimon said. “I just want to do the best I can for our clients, our country, our company.”Dimon has long stressed the importance of preparation, saying he always does pre-reads before meetings and believes in eliminating unnecessary meetings altogether.Meeting prep in the age of AIThe conversation also touched on how both executives are adjusting their meeting preparation habits as AI tools become part of their daily workflow. Both have traditionally stressed the value of reading materials ahead of meetings, but they suggested that habit may be shifting. Stankey said he's begun questioning whether reading is still the most effective way to absorb information, noting that engaging in a more conversational, dialogue-based format with AI now lets him process information faster when the conversation is well-directed. Dimon said he takes a similar approach, using AI tools like Gemini or Google to quickly dig into information as part of his meeting previews.Even so, the core principle hasn't changed for either executive: showing up prepared remains essential. Dimon has said that when he arrives at a meeting having already done his pre-reading, attendees get his full attention — and when a meeting isn't a productive use of people's time, he believes it shouldn't happen at all.Jamie Dimon's long history with meeting etiquetteDimon's focus on meeting discipline dates back decades. Early in his career, as a 28-year-old Harvard MBA working as an assistant to American Express president Sanford "Sandy" Weill, Dimon saw his role as primarily learning and observing, holding off on speaking until he had something valuable to contribute.That instinct to stay quiet and absorb information, however, likely wouldn't hold up well in Stankey's meeting culture — where a young employee following Dimon's old playbook might instead find themselves cold-called and expected to offer a point of view on the spot.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: A tech entrepreneur paid £555,000 for a derelict Welsh island fort; after a nearly five-year restoration, it is on the market for £3 million
articles.summary: UK News: A derelict 19th-century fortress sitting on a tiny island off the Pembrokeshire coast had no electricity, no running water and had been empty for 17 y.
articles.body: A derelict 19th-century fortress sitting on a tiny island off the Pembrokeshire coast had no electricity, no running water and had been empty for 17 years when technology entrepreneur Mike Conner bought it in 2017. He paid £555,000 for Thorne Island and then spent almost five years bringing the abandoned fort back to life. It now has 40 beds, four en-suite bathrooms and its own nightclub, and has been put back on the market for £3 million.How a 1850s Welsh island fort went from military base to abandoned ruinAccording to the data cited on island’s official site, Thorne Island lies near Milford Haven in Pembrokeshire and was originally built in the 1850s to protect the important naval port from French attacks. The 100-man fort later had a very different life, becoming a hotel in 1947 and hosting weddings, birthdays and stag parties.It was eventually sold in 1999, but attempts to bring it back into use failed. The island changed hands twice more in the years that followed, including a stint with a hotel group that abandoned plans for a costly relaunch, before Conner bought the listed building in May 2017, by which point it had sat largely derelict and overgrown for close to two decades.The first challenge was simply getting waterThe fort was a long way from being a functioning home when Conner arrived. There was no electricity or running water, while food and waste had to be transported between the island and the mainland.Even installing a working toilet became a major engineering job. According to the BBC, Conner had to cut through about 16ft (5m) of rock to reach a biodigester pump, a process that ultimately cost about £200,000.The restoration eventually took nearly five years, with six men living on the island for around four years while the work was carried out. Much of the equipment needed for the project had to be transported by helicopter because of the island's difficult location.The abandoned fort became a party spaceThe finished Thorne Island is very different from the waterlogged, empty building Conner purchased. The restored property now has 40 beds, four en-suite bathrooms and a nightclub, with the old military fort adapted for large gatherings and private events.The island had already developed a reputation as a party venue during its years as a hotel. Conner has continued that tradition, hosting events there himself, including celebrations for his 50th birthday. The island can accommodate around 800 people for events, although its current configuration provides sleeping space for about 40.Thorne Island is now on the market for £3 millionAfter years spent restoring the fort, Conner has decided to sell the unusual property. It is now being offered for £3 million, giving a new owner the chance to take over a private island with a restored historic fortress and facilities designed for large-scale entertainment.Conner told the BBC that he sees several possible futures for the site, from a tourist attraction to an events venue. He said the island could host what he described as an “unbelievable 24-hour experience”, with its isolation making it possible to hold large events without nearby neighbours.For Conner, the project was also more personal than simply renovating a property. He discovered during the restoration that he is a quarter Welsh, as his mother grew up at Upton Castle near Pembroke Dock. After years of construction, helicopter deliveries and engineering problems, the former technology entrepreneur now hopes someone else will decide what the unusual Welsh fortress becomes next.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ICE agent accused of shooting Venezuelan man arrested after 8 months
articles.summary: US News: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent accused of shooting a Venezuelan man was arrested in Minneapolis on Wednesday. The detention comes .
articles.body: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent accused of shooting a Venezuelan man was arrested in Minneapolis on Wednesday. The detention comes eight months after the incident in which he wounded the man and later lied to investigators, which became a flashpoint in US President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.Christian Castro turned himself in to agents of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension in downtown Minneapolis and was booked into the Hennepin County jail on an outstanding arrest warrant, ICE said.Castro is facing state assault charges over the January 14 shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan national. He is also accused of falsely reporting a crime after allegedly telling Department of Homeland Security officials that Sosa-Celis and others had attacked him with a snow shovel and broom. Video evidence later disproved that account, prosecutors said.Castro's arrest came after he was released on bond from federal custody earlier this month. He had been arrested in Texas on separate federal charges of making false statements to investigators about the shooting and was released with a GPS ankle monitor.His lawyer, Rolando Cantu, said Castro had always intended to face the charges in Minneapolis. He disputed prosecutors' claims that his client might flee to Mexico."He wants his day in court."Castro was expected to make his first state court appearance in Minneapolis on Thursday. He is due to appear in US District Court in neighbouring St Paul on Friday morning over the federal charges.Case linked to Operation Metro SurgeThe state case stems from a confrontation during Operation Metro Surge, the large-scale ICE deployment in Minneapolis as part of Trump's wider immigration crackdown.Castro allegedly shot Sosa-Celis in the leg through the door of his apartment while children were inside. The incident triggered protests and clashes between federal immigration agents and demonstrators.After the shooting, Castro returned to his home state of Texas, preventing Minnesota authorities from immediately arresting him. A warrant was later issued for his arrest.Texas Rangers eventually apprehended Castro. However, Texas Governor Greg Abbott declined to sign extradition papers sent by Minnesota Governor Tim Walz.Abbott questioned whether Castro could be considered a fugitive because the Department of Homeland Security had reassigned him to Texas after the Minneapolis shooting.Castro spent about 90 days in a Texas county jail and was released on August 27 after a federal judge rejected Minnesota's request for an immediate extradition order.He was arrested again in Texas after a federal grand jury indicted him in early September on charges of making false statements. The indictment marked the first US Justice Department prosecution of a federal law enforcement officer accused of wrongdoing linked to Operation Metro Surge.DHS has suspended Castro from ICE. A person familiar with the case has also said that a civil rights investigation into the shooting of Sosa-Celis was opened."Governor Abbott’s attempt to shield Mr. Castro from accountability has failed. We look forward to commencing our prosecution," Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said in a statement.

articles.title: MDR charges explained: Who will pay how much for UPI?
articles.summary: Money Matters News: From October 15, some UPI payments will stop being free for the people who receive them. The rules come from two places. On September 14, the Finance .
articles.body: From October 15, some UPI payments will stop being free for the people who receive them. The rules come from two places. On September 14, the Finance Ministry issued a notification under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. It kept UPI payments of up to Rs 2,000, and RuPay debit cards, free of any bank or system charge. A day later, the steering committee led by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) announced what happens above that line.Much of the reaction has been noise, so the details are worth setting out first.Who pays, and how muchThe charge is a merchant discount rate, or MDR. It is the fee a business pays for accepting a digital payment, and it is common with cards. For UPI, it will be 0.4 per cent on person-to-merchant (P2M) payments above Rs 2,000.In practice:PaymentCharge to the merchantRs 1,500 to a shopNilRs 2000 to a shopNilRs 3000 to a shopRs 12Rs 10,000 to a shopRs 40Rs 50,000 to a retailerRs 200Rs 75,000 or moreRs 300 (cap)On a Rs 1 lakh purchase, 0.4 per cent would be Rs 400, but the cap keeps it at Rs 300.Several things do not change:Transfers between individuals remain free at any amount. Sending Rs 20,000 to a friend costs nothing.Small merchants are protected. Those in the P2PM category, receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month through QR payments into their own accounts, pay nothing, even on a single payment above Rs 2,000. They move into the regular category only if they cross that limit for three consecutive months.AutoPay mandates for subscriptions, EMIs, insurance premiums and utility bills carry no prescribed MDR.Some sectors pay a flat Rs 5 on payments above Rs 2,000. These are railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and public utilities. A Rs 20,000 railway booking costs Rs 5, not Rs 80.Capital-market payments, to mutual funds, brokers and investment platforms, attract 0.02 per cent, also capped at Rs 300.The customer is not supposed to pay any of this. The government says banks have been told to ensure merchants do not pass the charge on, and that UPI apps cannot add platform fees. On paper, UPI stays free for the consumer.The case for the feeThe government's reasoning is not frivolous. UPI now handles about 2,400 crore transactions a month, worth close to Rs 30 lakh crore. A system that size needs constant spending on servers, fraud prevention, cybersecurity, dispute resolution and resilience. Since 2020, the basic merchant payment has earned banks and apps almost nothing, and subsidies have covered part of the gap. NPCI says the new revenue will stay within the ecosystem.The Rs 2,000 line was chosen with care. More than 95 per cent of UPI merchant payments are at or below it, so the tea stall and the kirana shop are untouched. The fee falls on larger commercial payments.So why the uproar over a charge this small?Small charges rarely stay smallThe first reason is precedent. The Securities Transaction Tax was introduced in 2004 alongside the removal of long-term capital gains tax on listed shares. In 2018, the capital gains tax returned. The STT stayed. Dividends, once taxed at the company level, are now taxed in shareholders' hands at slab rates. The concern is not today's Rs 40. It is that once a charging mechanism exists, the rate, the cap and the threshold can all change without much public debate.The second is pass-through. The rule says merchants should not add the fee to the bill, but merchants set their own prices. Anyone who has been told "2 per cent extra on card" knows how quickly such costs reach the customer. Retail prices are also rounded, so a Rs 20 cost can turn into a Rs 30 or Rs 50 increase. Once the charge disappears into the price, it becomes harder to see, and cash buyers end up paying it too.The third is cash. Some shopkeepers will offer a discount for cash rather than give up 0.4 per cent. Reports from Delhi suggest some traders have already started. For jewellers, furniture showrooms, contractors and clinics, that is an easy trade. It works directly against the formalisation that UPI has done so much to advance.The fourth is the threshold itself. A Rs 1,999 payment is free and a Rs 2,001 payment is not. A Rs 5,000 bill can become Rs 2,000, Rs 2,000 and Rs 1,000. The system will need monitoring to stop this, which brings its own cost.The fifth is how the numbers are presented. "Over 95 per cent of transactions stay free" counts payments, not money. Industry estimates suggest payments above Rs 2,000 make up about 4 per cent of merchant volume but roughly two-thirds of its value. Those larger payments are also where a digital trail matters most for tax.A rate that does not fit investingThe capital-market rate needs a second look. Money sent to a broker does not have to result in a trade, and the broker cannot pass the fee to the client. Consider 10,000 customers each making 50 transfers of Rs 2 lakh in a month without trading. At 0.02 per cent, that costs the broker about Rs 2 crore and earns nothing.Regulation makes this worse. SEBI's settlement rules require brokers to return unused client funds every month or quarter, and many clients send that money straight back, often by UPI. The broker pays each time. A modest MDR here is reasonable, but a cap of Rs 5 or Rs 10 per transfer would make more sense than Rs 300. Otherwise, zero-brokerage delivery trades may not last.The credibility problemAbout 15 months ago, the Finance Ministry dismissed reports of MDR on UPI as false and baseless, and reaffirmed its commitment to free digital payments. Governments are entitled to change their minds. But this reversal joins a longer list. Online real-money gaming was treated as a game of skill, then regulated, then banned within a few years. When policy moves this way, people stop trusting assurances, and a small fee draws a large reaction.What should happen nextUPI should not be starved of funds. If it needs money for security and resilience, the Budget can provide it openly, as it would for any critical infrastructure. If the MDR stays, three safeguards would help. The government should publish what the fee collects and where it goes. It should lower the cap for capital-market transfers. And it should commit to a review after a year, using data on cash usage and bill-splitting, before any rate or threshold is raised.UPI worked because accepting a payment cost almost nothing. The October fee is small. The rules that govern it should be clear, limited and hard to change quietly.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.
